title: Meadowgate Customer Intelligence — Account Health (Q3 2026)
author: Marcel Gomez
content:
h1. Q3 2026 Account Health — Meadowgate Customer Intelligence (meadowgate-ci.com)

h2. Executive summary
Meadowgate Customer Intelligence is *re-engaging after a prolonged budget and hiring freeze* that paused the original doc-search + support-agent program. The initial POC (Nov–Dec 2025) was technically successful (latency/throughput within targets for mid-sized traffic) and the primary gaps remain *commercial timing* and *internal sponsorship continuity*. 

As of Q3 2026, Procurement has indicated that limited new vendor spend can be approved for *time-bound pilots* if tied to measurable support deflection and cost controls. We have a credible path to restart via a short “POC refresh” focused on *cost model validation (caching/batching)*, *data residency confirmation*, and *security evidence completeness*.

*Health (Q3):* Amber (improving)

h2. Account snapshot
|| Field || Current (Q3 2026) || Notes / history ||
| Company ID | mhci-00472 | From CRM record | 
| Segment | Mid-market (201–1000 employees) | Unchanged | 
| Region | North America | Unchanged | 
| Primary use cases | Doc-search; Support-agent; Summarization | Unchanged | 
| Products in scope | Dedicated; Private; Optimize | Unchanged | 
| Deployment requirement | VPC | Still a hard requirement | 
| Security requirements (baseline) | SSO (SAML); SOC 2; Audit logging; Data residency; KMS | Additional asks added in Q3 (see Security) | 
| Key stakeholders | Data org + Support Ops + Procurement | Champion gap is narrowing (see Stakeholders) | 
| Competitive set | Anthropic; OpenAI; Cohere | Still active, but discount pressure has softened | 

h2. What changed since the last documented status (Mar 2026)
*Budget / procurement*
- The earlier CFO guidance (“no new vendor commitments until Q3 2026”) has shifted to: *pilot-only approvals allowed*, with strict spend caps and clear ROI gates.
- Procurement’s prior near-term preference for a competitor discount remains a reference point, but the evaluation has reopened due to renewed focus on *support cost reduction* and *knowledge base quality*.

*Internal champion situation*
- Original internal champion (Head of AI) remains departed (left Jan 2026).
- A new interim sponsor has emerged in the Data org (Director-level) to restart evaluation contingent on pilot scope discipline and measurable outcomes.

*Technical stance*
- Technical fit remains positive based on the original 4-week POC (Nov–Dec 2025).
- Meadowgate requested an updated cost model and performance notes tailored to their current ticket volume and KB growth rate (their volumes have increased since late 2025).

h2. Current status and forecast
*CRM stage (operational view):* Re-engaged / Pilot Planning (internal)

*Best-case close window:* 2026-10
- This replaces the prior target of 2026-06, which was invalidated by the freeze.

*Commercial shape (unchanged range, higher scrutiny):* 100k–250k ARR
- Finance remains cost-sensitive and expects a 12-month model with explicit assumptions and savings levers.

h2. Recent activity (key events)
- 2026-08-01 — Re-engagement call: Procurement confirmed pilot exception process; requested updated security packet and a not-to-exceed pilot SOW.
- 2026-07-22 — Solution review with Data + Support Ops: aligned on doc-search + support-agent as Phase 1; agreed to include caching/batching cost test plan.
- 2026-02-12 — Final POC review call: engineering confirmed latency & throughput within targets for mid-sized traffic.
- 2026-01-28 — Security SIG: requested SOC2 attestation + KMS integration details.

h2. POC recap (Nov–Dec 2025) — what still matters
*Scope*
- Doc-search + Support-agent workflows with VPC deployment requirement.

*Performance result (reference)*
- Median latency: ~120ms for 512-token generation on Dedicated profile during test load.

*Key takeaway*
- Engineering was satisfied; the blocking issues were organizational (freeze + champion loss) and commercial (cost model scrutiny + competitor discount comparisons).

h2. Q3 2026 risks and blockers
*1) ROI / cost model skepticism (High)*
- Meadowgate’s finance team is highly sensitive to inference spend and expects clear savings mechanisms.
- Mitigation: deliver a short-form model with explicit assumptions + show caching/batching impact and “Optimize” levers in a controlled pilot.

*2) Champion durability (Medium)*
- New sponsor is interim and needs quick wins.
- Mitigation: anchor on Support Ops outcomes (deflection, handle time reduction) with weekly readouts.

*3) Security packet completeness (Medium)*
- Baseline requirements remain: SOC2, SAML SSO, audit logging, data residency, KMS.
- New Q3 asks: a) most recent penetration test attestation/executive summary, b) DPA template review, c) audit log example events aligned to their incident response workflow.
- Mitigation: provide updated evidence bundle and a one-page “data residency statement (US-only)” consistent with our deployment option.

h2. Security and compliance status (Q3 2026)
*Confirmed required controls*
- SOC 2: required
- SSO (SAML): required
- Audit logging: required
- KMS: required (including key rotation expectations)
- Data residency: required (preference: US-only)

*Open items*
1. Provide updated SOC2 letter and bridge letter if applicable (latest period).
2. Provide pen test summary (or equivalent assurance) per Procurement request.
3. Provide an audit log sample aligned to: authentication events, admin actions, data access, and model invocation metadata.
4. Confirm KMS key rotation schedule (requested previously) and document how rotations are performed without service disruption.

h2. Next steps (Q3 execution plan)
*Goal:* Restart with a capped, time-bound pilot that re-validates cost and security assumptions and produces a procurement-ready package.

# Week 1: Send updated security evidence bundle + data residency statement (US-only) + draft DPA.
# Week 1–2: Deliver updated 12-month cost model (base + caching + batching + Optimize scenarios).
# Week 2: Pilot SOW draft with not-to-exceed spend cap and success criteria.
# Weeks 3–6: Pilot execution (VPC), weekly readout to sponsor + Support Ops.
# End of pilot: Decision meeting with Procurement + sponsor; convert to annual commitment if KPIs are met.

*Proposed pilot success criteria (draft)*
- Support deflection improvement demonstrated on a defined set of intents/articles.
- Measurable reduction in average handle time for supported workflows.
- Cost per resolved ticket stays within agreed threshold under realistic traffic.

h2. Recommended internal posture
Classify Meadowgate as *Warm — Reactivating* (not “closed-stalled”) given renewed procurement pathway and identified interim sponsorship. Continue to track competitor pricing pressure, but prioritize delivering a tight pilot frame with clear ROI gates.
